devices.numberingTitle: Which SDI connector is which output?
numbering: Output N is CasparCG channel N, which plays to DeckLink device N.
The Blackmagic driver decides the numbering, not the slot on the motherboard. With several cards the order follows the PCIe bus, which can change when you add or move a card.
A card can have more SDI connectors than outputs: fill + key or monitoring connectors belong to the same output. A Duo 2 or Quad 2 shows up as 2 or 4 separate devices.
Click Identify outputs: every output shows its own colour and a large number for 60 seconds. With fill + key, the key connector shows a white picture.
devices.roleHint_playout: Runs the schedule: clips, ad breaks and graphics. Link it to a channel under Channels.
devices.roleHint_live: Takes RTMP/SRT streams from events and plays them to its DeckLink output. The director cuts the ATEM to it when a live item is scheduled.
devices.roleHint_both: One node does both playout and live streams (one DeckLink output each).

remote.title: Remote sources
remote.intro: Live streams from outside the studio (a reporter, a remote studio, a church service) sent over RTMP or SRT. The studio node plays them to a DeckLink output, and you switch that output on air.
remote.listIntro: Every source has its own stream key. Give it only to the person who sends that stream.

remote.ingestFix: Run the studio node installer again with -ManagementHost set to this server, so the ingest server checks the stream keys at {{url}} and opens its status port (9997) to this server.

how.title: How remote sources work
how.intro: From the contributor's encoder to on air in five steps.

chain.ingest: Ingest server on the studio node

add.title: Add the source
add.text: Choose a name, the studio node and the DeckLink output that plays the stream, and the ATEM input that output is cabled to. A stream key is created for you.

send.title: Send the details
send.text: Open Connection details and send the server and stream key to the contributor. There are step-by-step instructions for OBS, vMix, Larix (phone) and ffmpeg.

check.title: Check the signal
check.text: As soon as the contributor starts streaming, the status changes to Receiving, with the codecs and the bitrate.

decklink.title: Put it on DeckLink
decklink.text: Send to DeckLink plays the stream on the SDI output, so you see it on the ATEM preview or multiview while it is not on air yet. If the stream drops and comes back, it is restarted automatically.

air.title: Switch it on air
air.text: In the Control room, click the source under Take live: the stream is started and the ATEM switches to its input. Back to schedule ends it. You can also put the source in a TV block to go live at a set time.

how.network: From outside your network, the contributor needs to reach the studio node on TCP 1935 (RTMP) or UDP 8890 (SRT): forward those ports on your router or firewall, or use a VPN, and set the public address under Devices → Studio nodes. Use SRT over the internet when you can: it copes much better with packet loss.

connect.title: Connection details: {{name}}
connect.intro: Send these details to the contributor. The stream key is a password: whoever has it can send a picture to this output.
connect.fullUrlHint: For apps with a single URL field.
connect.srtHint: Recommended over the internet (OBS 28+, vMix, Larix, hardware encoders).
connect.newKeyConfirm: Create a new stream key? The current key stops working for new connections; a contributor who is streaming now is not cut off until they reconnect.
connect.pullInfo: CasparCG pulls this source itself from {{url}}. The contributor does not need connection details.

obs.name: OBS Studio
steps: Settings → Stream: Service "Custom…".
Server: {{server}}
Stream key: {{key}}
Settings → Output (Advanced): encoder x264 or NVENC H.264, rate control CBR, bitrate 4000–6000 kbps, keyframe interval 2 s.
Settings → Video: 1920×1080, 25 or 50 fps (same as the channel). Click Start Streaming.
For SRT: Server = the SRT URL, leave the stream key empty.

vmix.name: vMix
steps: Click the cog next to Stream.
Destination: Custom RTMP Server.
URL: {{server}}
Stream Name or Key: {{key}}
Quality: H.264, 1080p, 4–6 Mbit/s, keyframe every 2 s. Click Start.
For SRT: choose SRT (Caller) as destination and paste the SRT URL.

larix.name: Larix (phone)
steps: Settings → Connections → New connection.
URL: {{server}}/{{key}}
Mode: Audio + Video. Save and select the connection.
Settings → Video: 1920×1080, 25 fps, 4–6 Mbit/s, keyframe 2 s.
Tap the record button to start streaming.
For SRT: paste the SRT URL as the URL instead.

ffmpeg.name: ffmpeg
steps: Send a file or capture device with the command below.
-re plays a file in real time; replace input.mp4 with your source.

encoder.title: Recommended encoder settings
items: Video H.264, audio AAC 48 kHz, 128–192 kbit/s
1920×1080 at the channel's frame rate (25 or 50)
Upload speed at least 1.5× the bitrate
Wired network instead of Wi-Fi where possible

clocks.title: Hour clocks
clocks.intro: An hour clock makes every hour start the same way: fixed blocks such as the ident, news or an ad break at the same minute, with programme windows in between.

clocks.help: Fixed blocks always start at their minute; a programme item never gets cut in half but moves to the next window. "Reserve" keeps a fixed amount of time for a block (e.g. 5:00 for ads), the rest is filled with the filler.
clocks.overbooked: The fixed parts are longer than an hour, or no time is left for the programme.
